patch.value: Docstring coverage gate: a lexer-backed, fail-closed documentation gate the fleet can share

pm-ops becomes the home of the fleet's documentation gate. Today no repo has one: the mandate requires full docstring coverage on all source, and the only attempt (an unmerged pm-changelog branch) is a line-regex scanner whose own header claims compiler-API rigor it does not have, leaves its internal-function rule unimplemented, and counts braces inside strings and template literals. Implement the analyzer once here, on the TypeScript lexer that ships with the repo's existing typescript devDependency, and expose it both as a pm-ops subpath export the other packages can call from a ten-line script and as a fleet-wide command.

A docstrings module is exported from pm-ops, backed by createScanner token streams rather than line regexes, so JSDoc inside strings, template literals and commented-out code can never satisfy it; every declaration form the finder does not recognise is reported as a violation rather than skipped; the internal-function rule is implemented rather than documented; negative-control tests prove the gate fails on each known-bad input; pm ops docstrings runs the same analyzer across one repo or the fleet; pm-ops passes its own gate
